bullets.title: NVDA 7-Day Losing Streak Ahead of Earnings; HBM Content Downgrade Flagged
bullets.body: NVDA fell for a 7th consecutive day—longest losing streak since 2022—ahead of Wednesday earnings that traders view as the key AI demand catalyst. Separately, SemiAnalysis issued a 'massive content downgrade alert': Rubin Ultra will ship with only 192GB HBM4 8-hi, well below the original 1TB preview and even below the standard Rubin's 288GB, raising questions about HBM demand trajectory. CDS on both NVDA and AVGO widened to new all-time highs daily.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera CPU Benchmarks at Hot Chips Criticized as 'Chart Murders'
bullets.body: Multiple conference attendees called NVDA's Hot Chips Vera CPU presentation misleading, describing the SPECrate benchmark comparisons as 'chart murders' using selectively presented metrics. SpaceXAI confirmed it will deploy Vera CPUs for agentic AI workloads, Grok inference, and Starmind AI satellite systems; separately, NVDA's Groq 3 LPX rack entered full production delivering 3,400 tokens/sec (4x Cerebras) and will deploy at Nebius later this year.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Delays Hybrid Bonding to HBM5 (2029-30); Intel's EMIB Wins HBM Packaging Business
bullets.body: SK Hynix confirmed hybrid bonding will not arrive for HBM4E, pushed to HBM5 at earliest in 2029-2030, capping HBM stack heights at 775 microns. Simultaneously, SK Hynix adopted Intel's EMIB advanced packaging for next-gen HBM—a win for INTC driven by continued TSMC CoWoS capacity constraints. MU warned at Hot Chips that AI compute triples every two years while HBM bandwidth grows less than 2x, widening the memory wall; HBM failures also cited in ~17% of Meta Llama 3 training interruptions.

bullets.title: AMD Crosses 30% x86 PC CPU Market Share for First Time; Server CPU at 46.4%
bullets.body: AMD broke above 30% of the x86 PC CPU market for the first time, with server CPU share reaching 46.4% vs Intel's 53.6%—Intel's lowest share since 1995. At Hot Chips, AMD's Helios double-wide rack architecture and shared memory fabric drew attention for future optical interconnect roadmap potential.

bullets.title: META Plans 'Hatch' AI Agent Platform Launch in Coming Weeks; October 'Watermelon' Model Next
bullets.body: META is preparing to launch 'Hatch,' a consumer AI agent platform (the consumer version of its internal OpenClaw agent) in the coming weeks, with its next AI model 'Watermelon' targeted for October. The move signals META's push into the rapidly expanding AI agent market.

bullets.title: BABA's HK$80B Share Sale Pressures Asian Equities; AI/Semiconductor Selloff Spreads Regionally
bullets.body: Alibaba's HK$80B share sale weighed on Hong Kong and mainland Chinese equities, while a broader AI and semiconductor selloff spread across Asia—South Korea equities particularly weak given chip exposure. Taiwan and Korea benchmark indices reversed intraday losses to close fractionally positive (+0.5% and +0.3% respectively), while the Nikkei fell 0.8% dragged by electronics.

bullets.title: Taiwan Indicts 9 People Including NVDA and SMCI Employees for Alleged Illegal Chip Exports
bullets.body: Taiwan prosecutors indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia and Super Micro, on charges related to illegal technology exports. No further financial details disclosed in available items.

bullets.title: TSLA Raises Cybertruck Prices 6-7% to Improve Margins at ~15K Unit Volumes
bullets.body: Tesla raised Cybertruck Standard and Premium AWD prices 6-7% (Dual Motor to $74,990; Premium AWD to $84,990) as low volumes (~15K units) make per-vehicle profitability 'nearly impossible.' Price increases are interpreted as margin-rescue moves given insufficient fixed-cost absorption at current sales pace. Tesla Semi factory inauguration in Nevada is planned for next month.

bullets.title: IREN Short Interest Surges to 32% at $40; Trade Idea: Short IREN, Long MSTR
bullets.body: IREN short interest jumped to 32% with the stock trading around $40. At least one fintwit trader is actively recommending a paired trade: short IREN, long MSTR for the rest of 2026.

bullets.title: Amazon Pinning Hardware Price Hikes Up to 60% on Memory Cost Surge; 'Project Tetromino' Robotics Warehouse
bullets.body: Amazon is implementing hardware price hikes of up to 60% attributed to memory cost surge, though industry consensus at Hot Chips expects the memory pricing cycle to change soon. Separately, Amazon is developing 'Project Tetromino,' a next-generation fully automated delivery warehouse using AI and robotics for complex last-stop package processing previously resistant to automation.

bullets.title: AAOI: TIA Supply Constraints Limiting 800G/1.6T Shipments; SMTC Reports Strong TIA Demand
bullets.body: AAOI flagged that TIAs and DSPs are limiting 800G/1.6T optical shipments, while SMTC reported TIA demand is 'exceptionally strong.' Author excited about SMTC prospects into 2027 ahead of SMTC's earnings. Ayar Labs removed both LITE and MTSI from its supply chain website, now listing only Sivers for laser suppliers—a potential negative read-through for those names.

bullets.title: NBIS Closes $5.75B Convertible Senior Notes Offering
bullets.body: Nebius Group closed a private offering of convertible senior notes with aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $5.75 billion, a significant capital raise for the AI infrastructure company.

bullets.title: APP, ABNB, OMC Hit 52-Week Milestones; SPY Closes Below 20-Day MA for First Time Since July
bullets.body: AppLovin (APP) hit a new 52-week low during Monday's session; ABNB and OMC hit new 52-week highs. SPY closed below its 20-day moving average for the first time since July, signaling potential downside momentum; NASDAQ ended down 0.71% and S&P 500 down 0.25%.

bullets.title: INTC Unveils Crescent Island GPUs for Agentic AI; Fund Discloses Long at $18 on Security/Nationalization Thesis
bullets.body: Intel unveiled Crescent Island GPUs with up to 32 Xe3P cores optimized for agentic AI, featuring low-cost LPDDR5X memory and up to 480GB capacity. Separately, a fund disclosed it went long INTC at $18 on a semiconductor security/nationalization thesis, characterized as not unreasonable versus neocloud-timed bets.

bullets.title: AMZN's Project Tetromino; INTU Reports After Close Tuesday
bullets.body: Intuit (INTU) reports earnings after the close Tuesday, per fintwit calendar tracking. Amazon separately advancing 'Project Tetromino' robotic warehouse design for tasks previously resistant to automation.

bullets.title: NVDA CDS at All-Time Highs Daily; AI Physical Bottleneck Thesis Gaining Traction
bullets.body: NVDA and AVGO credit default swaps have been reaching new all-time wide levels daily. One widely-followed account argues the AI bottleneck 'remains physical'—chip manufacturing capacity, advanced packaging, and fab investment are the limiting factor, not algorithms, which structurally supports semiconductor pricing power and capex intensity.

bullets.title: Germany Q2 GDP Beats at +1% YoY; IFO Confidence 88.8 vs 87.2 Est—Euro Macro Better-Than-Expected
bullets.body: Germany's Q2 GDP (SA QoQ) came in at +0.3% vs +0.2% estimate, and +1.0% YoY vs 0.9% expected. August IFO business confidence beat at 88.8 vs 87.2 consensus. Germany's 10-year yield hit its highest level in 15+ years, a notable macro headwind for global equity risk appetite.

bullets.title: Fed Rate Hike Odds Surge to 75% by Year-End; Druckenmiller Criticizes Bessent Bond Buyback Strategy
bullets.body: Market-implied odds of a rate hike by year-end rose to 75%. Stanley Druckenmiller—Bessent's former mentor—publicly criticized Treasury's bond buyback program as a 'mistake,' arguing markets are functioning normally and don't require intervention. Treasury's TGA reserves can buy time but not fiscal credibility, per separate commentary.

bullets.title: ARM AGI CPU Details Emerging; Multiple Competitive Arm Server Chips at Hot Chips 26
bullets.body: Detailed specifications of ARM's AGI CPU were disclosed at Hot Chips 26, where observers noted at least three (possibly four) distinct competitive Arm-based enterprise server chip offerings emerging—a signal of intensifying competition in the Arm server market.

bullets.title: BE Up 12% on Pelosi Disclosure; INTU Earnings Catalyst Tomorrow; DIS Executive Retirement Packages
bullets.body: Bloom Energy (BE) surged 12% after Nancy Pelosi disclosed a purchase of up to $12M in shares. Disney (DIS) is offering voluntary early retirement packages to executives as a cost-management measure. MTSI flagged by one research service as an emerging 'high-flyer' in data centers and space.
